question: can the BM/EEA decoder run in one 73-slot polynomial array, as the single-array contract assumes?
probe: build/dqi_single_array/packed_bm_probe.py (gitignored throwaway; imports nothing from the package)

three_region.note: C, B and one scratch copy -- the reference's live set; the ground-truth core

two_region_naive.note: C and B packed in one array, C' written in place, then C_old copied to B's region

two_region_swapped.note: roles exchanged each step so no data move is needed -- the packing 73 slots allow

weight_zero_trivial: the 6 decodes in each two-region arm are the weight-0 trials; neither arm decodes even a single error
why: C' = C + (d/b) x^m B reads C_old and B_old while B' = C_old writes C_old into B's region, so whichever region is written first destroys data the other still reads. Both orders were run; both fail at weight 1.
verdict: PACKING_ROUTE_CLOSED: peak 1,001 is unreachable by repacking the reference update. The contract's remaining route is re-deriving B_t by replay, which is a nested EEA rather than one division per round; that is unmeasured and carries its own falsifiers.
consequence: no single-array circuit was built, no registry entry was added, and dqi_builder still offers only proos_zalka and gluzdov_v6
